rag.question: What does ERR-PO-0412 mean and how do I fix it?

chunks.cite: QRC-03 v2026.1, p.1, § Quick reference: ERR-PO-0412 quick fix

lines.text: [Quick reference: ERR-PO-0412 quick fix · QRC-03 · v2026.1 · effective 2026-01-12]
Northbridge Cycles Ltd QRC-03 | v2026.1
Quick reference: ERR-PO-0412 quick fix
Field | Value
Document | QRC-03
Version | 2026.1
Effective | 2026-01-12
Owner | Purchasing key users
Status | CURRENT
Classification | INTERNAL
Steps
1. Read the code: ERR-PO-0412 TAX CODE DOES NOT MATCH SUPPLIER COUNTRY (NL).
2. The country in brackets is the supplier's.
3. Supplier outside the UK: change the tax code to VAT20-RC (or VAT5-RC for reduced-rate items).
4. UK supplier: use VAT20-UK.
5. Press F8 again.
Why it happens: Fetch always fills VAT20-UK, the code for a UK supplier, even when the supplier is in the Netherlands or
Poland.
Tips

chunks.cite: QRC-03 v2026.1, p.1, § Reading the country indicator

lines.text: [Quick reference: ERR-PO-0412 quick fix · QRC-03 · v2026.1 · effective 2026-01-12]
[Quick reference: ERR-PO-0412 quick fix › Tips › Reading the country indicator]
Reading the country indicator
• Look at the letters shown in brackets at the end of the error message.
• These letters show the country recorded on the supplier account in the system, such as NL for the Netherlands.
• Do not guess the tax treatment from memory; always confirm the location shown in the brackets before altering the
order line.
Selecting the correct tax code
• If the country indicator shows that the supplier is outside the UK, use the reverse charge tax code.
• Apply VAT20-RC for standard goods and materials, or VAT5-RC where the items qualify for the reduced rate.
• If the supplier is registered in the UK, select VAT20-UK instead.
• Check each line item on the purchase order individually, as split deliveries or mixed supplies must carry matching
codes throughout.

chunks.cite: QRC-03 v2026.1, p.1, § Recommitting the record

lines.text: [Quick reference: ERR-PO-0412 quick fix · QRC-03 · v2026.1 · effective 2026-01-12]
[Quick reference: ERR-PO-0412 quick fix › Tips › Recommitting the record]
Recommitting the record
• Once the tax code field has been amended, save the entry by pressing F8 again.
• Ensure the cursor remains in the line details area while pressing the key so the validation routine runs against the
amended field.
• If the system accepts the change, the status line will clear and the purchase order will proceed to the next stage.
Avoiding repeated errors
• Frequent occurrences of this message usually indicate that an overseas supplier has been set up with domestic
defaults on their master record.
• If you regularly raise orders for the same overseas vendor and the error persists on fresh orders, notify the purchase
ledger team so the underlying supplier profile can be reviewed.
• Never force an order through using domestic tax codes for an overseas account, as this distorts the tax returns.

answer.text:
**Meaning**
ERR-PO-0412 (`TAX CODE DOES NOT MATCH SUPPLIER COUNTRY`, revised from the previous wording `TAX REGION DOES NOT MATCH SUPPLIER STATE` [5]) means the tax code does not match the supplier’s country [5][6]. This occurs because Fetch always automatically enters `VAT20-UK` [4][6][8].

**How to Fix It**
1. Read the supplier country code shown in brackets at the end of the error message [3][4][5].
2. If the supplier is outside the UK, change the tax code to `VAT20-RC` (or `VAT5-RC` for reduced-rate items) [3][4]. If the supplier is UK-registered, select `VAT20-UK` [3][4].
3. Check each line item on the purchase order individually [3].
4. With your cursor in the line details area, press F8 again to re-run validation and save the record [2][4].

chain.question: Can I buy the battery packs from Brightcell Energy? They quote £104.

steps.why: Brightcell Energy is not onboarded in the supplier master, has no active rate contract, and is legally/operationally blocked from onboarding or receiving POs under POL-SUP-003, AMD-SUP-2026-02, and SO

chain.answer:
No, you cannot buy battery packs from Brightcell Energy today [1]. 

Brightcell Energy is not registered in the Ledgerline supplier master, and Northbridge Cycles cannot commence trading or issue purchase orders to an unlisted vendor until onboarding under SOP-PUR-001 is completed [1][3]. Furthermore, for lithium-cell parts (BAT-*), suppliers must hold a valid UN 38.3 compliance test certificate [1][2][3]. Brightcell Energy’s mandatory UN 38.3 report is currently undergoing laboratory renewal and is not expected until December 2026, which blocks qualification [1]. Under SOP-PUR-006, commercial price alone must never dictate vendor selection, and bids lacking a valid UN 38.3 certificate must be set aside [3].

The company is not currently set up in the Ledgerline ERP supplier master, meaning Northbridge Cycles cannot commence trading with them today[^r1][^r2]. Qualification is currently blocked because their mandatory UN 38.3 compliance test report is undergoing laboratory renewal and is not expected until December 2026[^r5][^r8].
